value.rationale: The question is motivated by quantum information transport and many-body flat-band protection: exact all-size spectral modes answer whether two hard-core excitations remain trapped on a dense, highly connected network. A striking structural dichotomy is established: the zero flat band traps a localized opposite-shore pair with a stationary weight approaching one, uniformly bounding its leakage at all times, while an entirely different pair of collective same-shore states undergoes perfect transfer if and only if the network is balanced. Exact frequencies, multiplicities, transport maxima, and unavoidable local transfer suppression have plausible use in designing controlled two-excitation networks. This is not merely a renaming of an arbitrary finite calculation.
